_help: A record build config: one JSON per record. The build script links the raw files of every unit from <data_root>/sources/<source> into <record>/<path>, converts their burst analyses into containers, links each measurement to its calibrations, and writes README.md, metadata.cif, origins.json and the checksums. Keys starting with _ are notes and are ignored.
label: harmonized layout
title: T4 Lysozyme Urea Unfolding — smFRET Construct S44pAcF/N132C
summary: Raw single-molecule FRET data of double-labeled T4 lysozyme (Alexa488-pAcF44 donor × Alexa647-Cys132 acceptor) at 0 M urea, each with the calibrations of its own setup and measurement day.

construct._help: What was measured: the protein, its labelling sites and dyes.
construct.name: S44pAcF/N132C
details: T4L (C54T/C97A) S44pAcF N132C. Donor: Alexa488-hydroxylamine conjugated to
p-acetyl-L-phenylalanine 44 (keto handle). Acceptor: Alexa647-maleimide on cysteine 132.

probes.description: Alexa Fluor 488 hydroxylamine conjugated to the keto group of 4-acetyl-L-phenylalanine 44 (oxime)
Alexa Fluor 647 maleimide conjugated to cysteine 132 (thioether)

construct.sequence_source: PDB 1L63 (T4 lysozyme, cysteine-free pseudo-wild type C54T/C97A), with the substitutions below

setups._help: One entry per instrument set-up and day; units name it in 'setup'.

instrument: Home-built confocal epi-illumination microscope (2014). TCSPC: PicoQuant
HydraHarp 400 in HT3 mode (Info file: reading routine 'PQ TH3R', laser rep.
15.62 ns). Eight detection channels: 2 colours (green, red) x 2 polarizations x
2 detectors per colour and polarization (dead-time-free); photons on routing

channels.name: green
channels.channels: 4 detectors: parallel and perpendicular, each split over 2 detectors (dead-time-free); routing 0-7 pairs 1:0, 3:2, 5:4, 7:6 (protocol)

channels.name: red
channels.channels: 4 detectors: parallel and perpendicular, each split over 2 detectors (dead-time-free)

units._help: A measurement: 'source' is under <data_root>/sources/, 'setup' names a setups entry, 'calibrations' (optional) the calibration folders of that setup it uses (default: all of them), 'trees' the analyses kept, 'flags' what the reviewer must check.
units.buffer: 0 M urea; 50 mM Na-phosphate, 150 mM NaCl (manuscript methods); plus 1 uM UNLABELED T4L wt* (no dye, invisible to detection; added as 1 uL per protocol to block surface adsorption); dye-labelled T4L S44pAcF/N132C at single-molecule (pM) dilution (protocol: 0.5 in 500, 0.5 in 500); room temperature
details: Background count rates (protocol of 2014-08-12, kHz): H2O green 0.831, red 0.601;
settings: Protocol: 8 channel set-up, Nunc chambers (8), 60 uW green at the objective.
flags: added measurement: not in the experiment list for #10, but documented in the 2014-08-12 protocol (S44 N132 (A488, A647) 0M urea, burstwise_All 0.0294#60) -- confirm

units.content: buffer, 0 M urea (50 mM Na-phosphate, 150 mM NaCl): background
clean H2O: scatter and instrument response; the Green Scatter of every 2014 burst analysis (Paris Info: irf/Split_irf-*_10.dat, *_32.dat)
flags: role from the analysis' Info file (Green Scatter) -- confirm this folder is the water measurement

zenodo._help: The Zenodo metadata (reviewed as an item before upload). Never name the container format here.
zenodo.title: T4 lysozyme urea unfolding — single-molecule FRET (MFD), construct S44pAcF/N132C (example, 0 M urea): raw TTTR data, burst analysis and calibrations
zenodo.description: Raw single-molecule FRET data (multiparameter fluorescence detection, TTTR) of double-labelled T4 lysozyme S44pAcF/N132C (Alexa Fluor 488 donor at 4-acetyl-L-phenylalanine 44, Alexa Fluor 647 acceptor at cysteine 132; cysteine-free pseudo-wild type C54T/C97A) at 0 M urea, with the burst analysis of every measurement in one analysis container per measurement and the calibrations of each setup and measurement day. Metadata: flrCIF/mmfdb metadata.cif (validated against the mmCIF, IHM, IHM-FLR and mmfdb dictionaries); provenance in origins.json; checksums in manifest_sha256.csv. Part of the T4L urea-unfolding series.
